content.text:
The drawing breaks down into four parts.

- **Piperidine amidine:** a piperidine ring whose nitrogen is bonded to C(=NH), which is attached to a para-substituted benzene ring.
- **First amide:** the benzene ring carries a C(=O)NH group on the opposite side, and that NH is attached to the central ring.
- **Central ring:** a benzene ring with the NH at C1, the C(=O)NH-pyridyl group at C2 (adjacent), and the OMe on the ring carbon that is para to the NH. In the drawing, the ring carbon bearing NH is at the bottom left of the ring, the carbon bearing the carboxamide is at the bottom right, and OMe sits at the top right. The OMe carbon is therefore meta to the carboxamide carbon and para to the NH carbon.
- **Pyridine:** attached through its 2-position to the amide NH, with Cl at the 5-position. The ring is N1, C2 (bearing NH), C3, C4, C5 (bearing Cl), C6.

Checking the central ring positions: C1 carries NH, C2 carries the carboxamide, C3 is the CH next to it, C4 carries OMe, C5 is CH, and C6 is CH. This puts OMe para to NH, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: N=C(N1CCCCC1)c1ccc(cc1)C(=O)Nc1ccc(OC)cc1C(=O)Nc1ccc(Cl)cn1
